title: Legacy CRM Admin Guide — Territory Administration and Account Alignment
summary: The territory administration framework for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering Enterprise Territory Management with model-based territory hierarchies, assignment rules for user-to-territory and account-to-territory mapping, account alignment with affiliation-based rules, and the legacy Territory Management 1.0 compatibility layer.

findings.enterprise_territory_management: Enterprise Territory Management (ETM) provides a model-based approach to organizing territories. Administrators create territory types (classifications like Region, District, Area), then build a territory model as a hierarchical tree of territory records. Each model progresses through lifecycle stages: Planning (draft configuration), Active (live assignment processing), and Archived (historical reference). Only one territory model can be active at a time. Territory customization allows administrators to add custom fields to territory records for metadata like geographic boundaries, market segments, or capacity targets. The activation process validates the entire hierarchy before committing changes.
findings.territory_assignment_rules: Assignment rules govern how users and accounts map to territories. User-to-territory assignment links field representatives to one or more territories, controlling which accounts and data they can access on mobile devices. Account-to-territory assignment uses rule-based automation: administrators define criteria (account attributes like specialty, address, classification) that determine which territory an account belongs to. Rules execute hierarchically — parent territory rules can cascade to child territories, and child territories can override parent rules. Rule jobs process assignments in batch, with execution logs tracking which accounts were assigned, moved, or excluded.
findings.account_alignment_framework: Account Alignment extends basic territory assignment with sophisticated rule processing. Alignment rules define criteria-based matching (account fields, geographic proximity, specialty filters) while assignment rules handle the actual territory placement. Affiliation-based alignment uses organizational relationships — if a healthcare provider is affiliated with a healthcare organization already in a territory, the provider can be automatically aligned to the same territory. Rule jobs execute alignment processing with configurable scheduling. The hierarchy execution model processes rules top-down through the territory tree, allowing each level to refine assignments. Administrators can exclude specific accounts from rule processing and configure territory-level quantity limits to cap how many accounts a territory can hold.
findings.legacy_territory_management: Territory Management 1.0 provides backward compatibility for organizations that have not migrated to Enterprise Territory Management. This legacy model uses a simpler flat or two-level territory structure without the full model lifecycle. Manual user management allows direct user-to-territory assignment without rule automation. Organizations can migrate from 1.0 to ETM through a structured migration path that maps existing assignments to the new model-based hierarchy.
findings.local_administration: Local Administration delegates territory management to regional administrators. Administrators can set divisions (organizational groupings) and assign specific territories for local administrators to manage. This distributed administration model allows regional managers to handle day-to-day territory adjustments without requiring central administrator involvement for every change.

title: Legacy CRM Admin Guide — Product and Message Administration
summary: The product and message administration framework for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering multi-level product hierarchy management, territory-based product alignment with inclusion and exclusion controls, product messaging configuration for call interactions, product restrictions with delta job processing, and signature requirements for call documentation.

findings.product_hierarchy_management: Products are organized in a multi-level hierarchy that supports search, creation, editing, and deletion operations. Lot management associates products with specific sample lots for inventory tracking — each lot has a unique identifier, expiration date, and quantity attributes. Territory allocations for sample orders control how much of each product a territory can order during a given period. Product-to-territory alignment defines which products are available in each territory, with support for inclusion rules (explicitly adding products) and exclusion rules (removing products from child territories that would otherwise inherit them from parent territories).
findings.product_message_administration: Product messages represent the key talking points and detail aids that field representatives use during provider interactions. Administrators create messages, configure healthcare provider reaction capture (enabling or hiding reaction tracking), and manage message lifecycle through activation and deactivation. Messages support grouping and sorting on the call form to organize the discussion flow. Territory alignment controls which messages are available in each territory. Detail priorities define the recommended ordering of messages during a call. Messages can be associated with brand-indication pairs and therapeutic area classifications, allowing representatives to access contextually relevant content based on the products being discussed.
findings.product_restrictions_framework: Product restrictions control which products can be discussed or sampled at the account, territory, and product level. The restriction framework uses delta jobs — incremental processing runs that detect changes since the last execution and update restriction states accordingly. Activation controls when restrictions take effect. Account-level restrictions block specific products for individual accounts (regulatory holds, compliance issues). Territory-level restrictions remove products from entire territories (market withdrawal, supply constraints). Product-level restrictions apply global constraints across all territories (recall, regulatory suspension).
findings.call_form_configuration: Product signature configuration determines whether electronic signatures are required when products are discussed or sampled during a call. The products-on-call-form ordering controls the display sequence of products during call documentation. Product quantity defaults pre-populate suggested quantities for sample disbursement, reducing data entry during field visits. These configurations work together to streamline the call documentation workflow while maintaining compliance requirements.

title: Legacy CRM Admin Guide — Ratings, Profiling, and Territory Sales Data
summary: The ratings and profiling administration framework for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering configurable rating layouts with multiple display types, profiling questions with attachment support, team-based and address-level ratings, response sharing across users, rating history tracking, and territory-level sales data integration.

findings.rating_layout_architecture: Ratings use a configurable layout system where administrators create rating layouts, define sections within them, and add individual rating elements. Each layout maps to specific account profile pages. Sections support translation for multi-language deployments and can be added or reorganized within layouts. Rating elements support multiple display types (numeric scales, picklists, text entry, checkbox groups) that determine how field representatives interact with the rating during account visits. The layout configuration drives both the mobile and web rendering of the rating interface.
findings.atp_and_orchestration: Account Targeting Priority (ATP) creation enables administrators to generate prioritized account lists based on rating scores and business rules. Custom ATP fields extend the standard targeting model with organization-specific attributes. Orchestration values define the scoring algorithms and weighting factors that convert raw rating data into actionable prioritization scores. Specific products can be linked to ratings to create product-specific targeting — for example, a provider's prescribing propensity for a particular therapeutic area affects their priority score for that product's representative.
findings.advanced_rating_types: Team-based ratings allow multiple users to contribute to a single account's rating profile, aggregating inputs from medical science liaisons, sales representatives, and key account managers into a unified view. Account address ratings apply ratings at the address level rather than the account level, supporting scenarios where a provider's behavior differs across practice locations. Profiling-question-based ratings use structured questionnaires to capture qualitative provider insights — questions support attachment uploads for supporting documentation. Standalone profiling questions can exist outside the rating framework for ad-hoc data collection. Response sharing enables cross-user visibility of profiling answers, allowing team members to see what others have captured.
findings.history_and_migration: Rating history tracking maintains a chronological record of rating changes, enabling trend analysis and audit trails for compliance purposes. Version migration tools support upgrading rating configurations between platform releases, preserving existing data while adapting to new rating framework capabilities. Territory-level sales data configuration integrates external sales performance metrics (prescription data, market share figures) into the CRM, making this data available alongside rating information on account profiles for a complete provider engagement picture.

title: Legacy CRM Admin Guide — CLM Presentation Administration and Content API
summary: The CLM presentation administration framework for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering sequence and presentation configuration with bulk operations, territory-based content alignment, CLM settings for training and engagement control, content filtering and rating, interactive features (laser pointer, drawing, messaging platform sharing), and the Content API with v1 and v2 endpoint specifications.

findings.sequence_and_presentation_management: Sequences organize multiple presentations into recommended interaction flows for field representatives. Administrators edit sequence metadata, associate products and messages with sequences, configure reporting fields for analytics, and manage sequence lifecycle through activation and deactivation. Asset management links supporting materials to sequences. Presentation configuration supports individual and bulk operations: create single presentations or bulk upload batches via file import, bulk update metadata across multiple presentations, and bulk edit properties. Presentations support reporting field configuration, territory alignment (controlling which territories can access which content), availability date windows, email distribution, and lifecycle management. Custom presentations allow administrator-defined content packages, while favorites let users bookmark frequently used presentations.
findings.clm_settings_and_controls: CLM settings govern platform-wide presentation behavior. Training mode enables practice sessions without recording engagement data. Content locking prevents representatives from skipping required slides. Geolocation tracking captures where presentations are delivered. Date validation in meetings enforces that CLM interactions are recorded with accurate timestamps. Next Best Message integration suggests optimal content based on account context. Advanced account search helps representatives find the right provider during unplanned interactions. Lock screen prevents device sleep during presentations. Sequence name display and territory attribute restrictions control what representatives see. Call presentation records link CLM engagement data to call records for compliance reporting.
findings.content_discovery_and_interaction: Filtering supports both manual criteria (by product, therapeutic area, territory) and recommended filters that use algorithmic suggestions based on account context. Content rating allows representatives to provide feedback on presentation effectiveness. Interactive features include a laser pointer for emphasis during remote presentations, drawing tools for annotation, messaging platform sharing for digital distribution, and web-based CLM player for browser-based content delivery. Email from CLM enables sending presentation content directly to providers. Survey response capture from within CLM presentations integrates profiling data collection into the content flow. Medical inquiry creation from CLM allows representatives to initiate clinical question workflows during a presentation.
findings.content_api_specification: The Content API provides programmatic access to CLM assets in two versions. Version 1 offers endpoints for CLM content retrieval, field email template access, and document management operations. Version 2 introduces enhanced CLM endpoints with expanded metadata, improved filtering, and bulk operations, plus enhanced field email endpoints with template versioning and delivery tracking. The Document Management endpoint (v1 only) handles file upload, retrieval, and deletion for content assets. A detailed v1 versus v2 comparison documents the differences in request format, response structure, authentication requirements, and capability coverage to guide integration decisions.

title: Legacy CRM Admin Guide — Analytics Engine (Next Best Customer/Message) and Next Best Action
summary: The analytics engine administration for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering the cloud-hosted computation platform for Next Best Customer and Next Best Message metrics, metric configuration across account, product, and custom dimensions, data synchronization scheduling, error monitoring, and the Next Best Action recommendation framework.

findings.analytics_platform_provisioning: The analytics engine runs on a cloud-hosted computation platform that requires dedicated instance provisioning. Setup involves configuring the connection between the CRM platform and the analytics service, establishing data synchronization channels, and activating the computation environment. The provisioned instance processes CRM data to generate account-level and product-level metrics that drive field force prioritization decisions.
findings.metric_configuration_taxonomy: Metrics fall into several categories based on their data source and calculation method. Account-level metrics include: Boolean (binary flags like active prescriber status), Variable Days (time-windowed calculations like days since last interaction), Percentage (ratio calculations like market share), and Fixed Value (static thresholds). Product-level metrics include: Boolean (product-specific flags), Fixed Value (product thresholds), Average (rolling averages like average prescription volume), Change in Value (period-over-period deltas), and Trend Slope (directional trend indicators). Multi-channel messaging metrics track engagement across digital channels. Custom metrics allow administrator-defined calculations using formulas that combine standard metric inputs. Prescription data options and defined daily dose options configure how pharmaceutical dispensing data feeds into metric calculations.
findings.next_best_message_metrics: Next Best Message metrics analyze historical engagement patterns to recommend which content or talking points to present during provider interactions. These metrics consider past CLM presentation engagement, email open and click rates, provider response patterns, and product discussion history. The recommendation engine uses these signals to suggest the most effective content sequence for each provider-product combination.
findings.data_sync_and_monitoring: Data synchronization configuration defines how frequently CRM data flows to the analytics engine and how computed metrics flow back. Schedule management controls when sync jobs execute, balancing data freshness against system load. Three monitoring surfaces track system health: Sync Log (data transfer status and record counts), Run Log (computation job execution and duration), and Error Log (failed calculations, data quality issues, and system exceptions). Custom settings provide fine-grained configuration of computation parameters. Limits management controls resource consumption and processing thresholds.
findings.next_best_action_framework: Next Best Action extends beyond content recommendations to suggest the optimal engagement action for each provider — whether to call, email, send digital content, or defer contact. The recommendation considers provider preferences, regulatory constraints, recent interaction history, territory workload, and business objectives. Configuration includes the AI and ML settings that tune recommendation sensitivity, custom settings for organization-specific business rules, and limits that bound recommendation generation.

title: Legacy CRM Admin Guide — Remote Detailing and Field Email Administration
summary: The remote detailing and field email administration framework for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering remote call configuration with audio/video/chat/SIP capabilities, content adaptation for remote delivery, the field email lifecycle including template management, opt-based sending controls, email queue monitoring, and bulk email capabilities.

findings.remote_detailing_configuration: Remote detailing enables virtual provider interactions without in-person visits. Configuration includes enabling the remote detailing capability at the org level, setting up remote call parameters (session URL generation, session key management, email invitation templates), and establishing the Connected App for OAuth-based authentication. The content adaptation tool reformats CLM presentations for optimal remote delivery, adjusting layouts and interactions for screen-sharing contexts rather than in-person tablet presentations.
findings.remote_session_capabilities: The remote session infrastructure supports multiple communication channels: audio (voice calls), video (face-to-face video), chat (text messaging during sessions), and SIP (Session Initiation Protocol for enterprise telephony integration). Server provisioning configures the infrastructure that hosts remote sessions. Attendee status tracking monitors participant engagement during sessions. CLM presentations can be delivered through the remote player, maintaining engagement tracking and slide-level analytics. The system supports migration from legacy remote call implementations to the current remote engagement architecture.
findings.field_email_template_management: Field email administration covers the complete template lifecycle: uploading HTML email templates, managing embedded attachments and images, editing template content and metadata, aligning templates to territories (controlling which representatives can use which templates), creating new template versions while preserving historical send data, configuring availability windows, and managing activation and deactivation. Templates support content security policy trusted site configuration for external resources. Filtering and sender configuration controls which email addresses appear as senders. Opt-based controls respect provider communication preferences — administrators can configure email address availability based on opt-in status, enable bypass for certain opt categories, and disable email validation checks when providers have not explicitly opted out.
findings.email_operations_and_queue: Email settings control send-to behavior: sending to healthcare organizations (not just individual providers), copying colleagues on field emails, scheduling future sends, and language selection for multi-locale templates. Email jobs process scheduled sends, with user profile image integration for personalized sender identification. The email queue provides operational visibility with filtering, searching, and sorting of queued messages, status tracking (pending, sent, delivered, bounced, failed), individual record inspection, and administrative actions (cancel, retry, prioritize). Web-based email sending extends the capability beyond mobile, and bulk email enables mass distribution for targeted campaigns. Calendar event creation via ICS file attachment allows field emails to include meeting invitations.

title: Legacy CRM Admin Guide — Sample Management, Field Coaching, and Territory Plans
summary: The sample management, field coaching, and territory plan administration for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering the complete sample lifecycle with advanced limit templates, field coaching event workflows with form-based evaluation, and territory business plan configuration.

findings.sample_management_administration: Sample management administration encompasses process configuration, permission set assignment, and operational controls. Additional fields can be added to sample order, transaction, and inventory header records for organization-specific tracking. Product availability configuration controls which products appear in sample transaction forms. Date and time field configuration enables precise timestamp recording for shipment receipt. Administrators can limit available products by active sample lot allocation — only products with active inventory lots appear for disbursement. Transaction blocking and warning controls allow administrators to block or warn users for specific transaction types (return, transfer out) based on business rules. Audited inventory submission controls govern the formal inventory verification process. Sample orders page configuration customizes the mobile sample ordering experience. Address management and display configuration controls how provider addresses appear during sample transactions. Management jobs handle batch processing for inventory operations. Signature audit provides compliance verification of captured signatures. Custom settings and trigger handlers extend the sample management framework with organization-specific logic.
findings.sample_limits_framework: Sample limits enforce regulatory quantity restrictions on sample disbursement. The framework uses templates — administrators create limit templates that define rules and operations (maximum quantities per time period, per product, per account). Templates can be cloned for rapid deployment across product lines. Rules are assigned to specific products and can be viewed or deleted individually. Generic template limits provide organization-wide defaults. Segmentation divides accounts into groups with different limit thresholds (high-volume prescribers may have higher limits than low-volume). Limit initialization creates baseline records for all accounts, with automatic initialization for newly created accounts. Advanced template capabilities include: error type configuration for cloned templates, template summary views for operational oversight, per-product template limits, consideration of shipped quantity for direct-to-physician orders, disbursement validation against lot allocation, and DTP sample validation against product territory allocation. Delta jobs and batch processing controls optimize limit recalculation performance.
findings.field_coaching_administration: Field coaching enables managers to observe and evaluate field representative performance during provider interactions. Permission configuration controls who can create and participate in coaching events. Custom settings define organization-specific coaching parameters. Event statuses and workflow flow govern the coaching lifecycle: scheduled, in-progress, pending evaluation, completed. The coach-employee workflow supports same-user scenarios (self-evaluation) and modification controls for self-assessment. Block employee change after creation prevents reassignment of coaching events. View previous evaluation data allows managers to reference historical assessments. Assignment limits restrict coaching to subordinate users within the management hierarchy. Overlap prevention blocks scheduling conflicts between coaching events. Layout configuration customizes the coaching form display. Form template and question management defines the evaluation criteria — administrators create form templates, add questions with scoring rubrics, and assemble them into evaluation instruments. Feature activation after platform upgrades ensures coaching capabilities remain functional across releases.
findings.territory_plans_and_document_management: Territory plans link business objectives to field execution. Territory business objectives can be connected to individual calls, making plan targets visible during daily call activities. Business to-do filtering by call details allows representatives to see relevant plan tasks based on the calls they are making. Plan activation controls when territory plans become effective. The administration guide also covers publication record management (tracking document versions and approvals) and document approval workflows that govern content lifecycle for regulated materials.
